sprint: THE REACH SPRINT (V35) — THE HALT, HONORED A SECOND TIME. V34's gate re-pinned the Halt: if IN2 is unperformed at V34's close, V35 is validation-only TOO, and the gate must present whether the product has a user at all. V34's terminal marker reads realLineageCount:0 — IN2 remains unperformed, the Halt binds, V35 ships ZERO new product capability. What ships instead is the END of four unfalsifiable claims the engine had been making about itself: a check that never executed (the frozen core's DSR/PSR/PBO cross-check), a gate with a permanently-red sub-check every marker called green, a census-never-taken of whether any wall can fail, and a kill-criterion weighed against a number that could not have been non-zero (no binary, no install, no publication). ONE law: X-REACH — an instrument that cannot return the negative result is not an instrument.

xReach.a_aCheckThatCannotFailIsNotACheck: A CHECK THAT CANNOT FAIL IS NOT A CHECK. Every wall must be shown to FAIL on a seeded negative — and the seeded negative must be the ORIGINAL DEFECT the wall was minted to catch, named in the pins, not an arbitrary mutation. A wall with no demonstrated failure is a DECORATION, and decorations are counted as NOT HELD (X-SHOWN(b)). Walls whose negative is structurally unrepresentable (a grep-wall for a daemon that must not exist in the tree) are enumerated as a reasoned EXEMPT class — never silently excused. RP-1: most of S1-S92 have NO recorded originating defect; a census that pretends to know why 99 walls exist is exactly the unfalsifiable claim this sprint was minted to end — so a fourth bucket, ORIGIN-UNRECORDED, is counted and expected to be large, and a wall in it shows whatever negative exists explicitly labelled NOT-PROVEN-to-be-the-original-defect.
xReach.b_aCrossCheckThatDoesNotExecuteIsNotAChe: A CROSS-CHECK THAT DOES NOT EXECUTE IS NOT A CHECK — IT IS AN ABSENCE WEARING A CHECK'S NAME. The frozen core's DSR/PSR/PBO cross-check had never executed in the audited record. Therefore D33 is UNSIGNABLE while S94 is red — not advice to the Operator but a structural precondition asserted by a wall, and the countersign package must refuse to present D33 as signable until the cross-check is green. RP-2: the cross-check is NEVER vendored, stubbed, mocked, or reimplemented — a mocked cross-check is worse than an absent one; if it cannot install, S94 stays RED, the blocker is named in one actionable sentence, and D33 is pinned UNSIGNABLE anyway (the law's purpose is served by the honest red).
xReach.c_aGateExpectedToBePartiallyRedIsNotAGat: A GATE EXPECTED TO BE PARTIALLY RED IS NOT A GATE. verify is green end-to-end, or its failing sub-check is RETIRED WITH DISCLOSURE. And green is a DERIVED VALUE, never a typed word — a marker's verify slot carries the command's exit code and a per-sub-check status list, so that no human sentence can assert a health the machine did not observe. RP-6/attack-6: the lesson of V33->V34 (shapes not substrings) applied to the project's own reporting — a wall asserts that no marker types the word green for a command whose exit code was non-zero.
xReach.d_aNumberThatCouldNotHaveBeenNonZeroIsNo: A NUMBER THAT COULD NOT HAVE BEEN NON-ZERO IS NOT A MEASUREMENT. A metric may be weighed against the kill-criterion only when the mechanism by which it could have been non-zero exists and is shown. Zero users with zero doors is not evidence of no demand; it is evidence of no door. Firing a falsification instrument on an unfalsifiable number is the precise inversion of everything this project is.
xReach.e_reachIsAFactStructuralNeverSurveyed: REACH IS A FACT, and it is STRUCTURAL, never surveyed. reach = { installPath, firstRunSeconds, published, reachableHumans } where reachableHumans = published ? UNJUDGEABLE : 1. ORGANON does not guess how many strangers exist. If it is unpublished, exactly one human can reach it, and that human is the Operator. If it is published, the count is UNJUDGEABLE and says so. RP-4: published is DERIVED from the git remote state (is this commit reachable from any remote ref?), NEVER a declared constant — a declared published flag is the same defect X-RECKON was minted to kill, reintroduced in a new field.
xReach.f_distributionIsNotCapability: DISTRIBUTION IS NOT CAPABILITY. Compiling the same code into a binary and writing an install line adds no module, no surface, no screen, no law, no dependency, and no verdict. It changes only whether the existing capability can be REACHED. Disclosed as D49, unsigned, against the Halt's letter — and the Operator may strike it (PART A' attack #3, where this argument is attacked properly rather than assumed). The narrowing the attack forces is TAKEN: the binary ships and nothing else.

censusSchema.rule: S93 — X-REACH(a) made mechanical. Every wall S1-S92 is bucketed by a pure read over a COMMITTED wall catalog; a wall referenced in test/ with no catalog entry FAILS the battery (RP-6 — a living wall, not a document). The census is committed content-hashed to data/honesty/falsifiability-census.json and the number of DECORATIONS found is stated out loud.

buckets.DEMONSTRATED: a seeded negative exists AND it is the ORIGINAL defect the wall was minted for (the defect is quoted from the build log that minted it, e.g. a W-xxNN tag; the negative reproduces THAT defect).
buckets.WEAK: a seeded negative exists but it is an arbitrary mutation, not the original defect -> STRENGTHEN it to the original defect or NAME it.
buckets.EXEMPT: the negative is structurally unrepresentable (a grep-wall for a daemon that must not exist in the tree) -> reasoned, enumerated, and COUNTED; a rising exempt count across sprints is itself a finding.
buckets.ORIGIN_UNRECORDED: RP-1 (the CRITICAL Part-F correction) — the wall has NO recorded originating defect in any build log; the census shows whatever negative exists, explicitly labelled NOT-PROVEN-to-be-the-original-defect. It is a fourth bucket, it is counted, and it is expected to be large. A census that pretends to know why 99 walls exist is the unfalsifiable claim this sprint was minted to end.

censusSchema.livingWall: RP-6 — Falsify.census() is a pure read over the wall catalog; the catalog is committed; a wall id appearing in test/ titles that is absent from the catalog FAILS the census battery on the next run. The census is regenerated by the battery, never written by hand, so it cannot rot the way the golden-move discipline rotted.
censusSchema.anyWallInNoBucketFails: a wall assigned to none of the four buckets FAILS the battery (X-REACH(a)).

verifyObjectSchema.rule: X-REACH(c) — the marker's verify slot is a DERIVED OBJECT { exitCode: n, subchecks: [{ name, status, detail }] }, produced by Verify.run() reading the command's real exit code and per-sub-check results. NEVER the typed word green.
verifyObjectSchema.wall: S95 — a marker that types the word green (case-insensitive) for a command whose exitCode was non-zero FAILS the battery. Marker.validate gains a verify-object branch; the terminal marker carries the object, not a sentence.

reachFact.publishedDerived: RP-4 — published is DERIVED: HEAD's commit is reachable from a remote ref (git branch -r --contains HEAD non-empty) => true, else false. A declared constant is FORBIDDEN and is the X-RECKON defect reintroduced. The honest limit: remote-tracking refs reflect the last fetch; the unpublished case (empty) cannot false-positive to published without an actual push.

The same code, compiled, keyless, offline on first run, with the Operator console locked behind a flag. Adds no module/surface/screen/law/dependency/verdict. Attack #3 partly LANDS (a binary lets a stranger run ORGANON without a dev toolchain — that IS reach): answered on the Halt's own purpose — the Halt exists to stop engineering AHEAD of validation, and a binary is the PRECONDITION of validation for anyone but the Operator; refusing it makes the Halt self-sealing. The narrowing is taken: the binary and NOTHING else. operatorSigned=false; the Operator may strike it and V35 still delivers Phases 1-3 and 5 whole.
deviations.D50: DISCLOSED — THE KILL-CRITERION IS DEFERRED, HASH-PINNED, WITH ITS ENDING CONDITION. The kill-criterion (8b4e094b) may be weighed on the cycles-run number WHEN AND ONLY WHEN: (i) a binary exists, (ii) an install path exists, (iii) the tree is PUBLISHED (derived, not declared), and (iv) a stated observation window has elapsed since publication. RP-5: the window is stated NOW as a number — 90 days from the publication commit, or 30 days from the first external clone, whichever is sooner. When all four hold, the number is a measurement; until then it is the Operator's calendar. A deferral with a machine-checkable ending condition is a pre-registered exit criterion — the instrument this product sells (ORGANON applying X-MANIFEST to itself). operatorSigned=false.

haltRePinned.rule: THE HALT IS RE-PINNED A THIRD TIME, NOT RETIRED. IN2 remains unperformed (realLineageCount:0 at V34's close), so V35 is validation-only and ships zero new product capability. The kill-criterion's question — whether the product has a user at all — is now DUE, and it is answered honestly: not fired, not dodged, but shown to be UNANSWERABLE by the current number because the product has never been reachable by anyone but the Operator (no binary, no install, no publication).
haltRePinned.twoPens: reach carries TWO blocking Operator acts, not one: IN2 (perform it) and PUBLICATION (decide it). The kill-criterion cannot honestly fire until BOTH are discharged (X-REACH(d)); firing it before would be the project's own X-HONEST violation.
haltRePinned.terminalClause: IF V36 OPENS WITH IN2 UNPERFORMED AND THE TREE UNPUBLISHED, the Operator has answered the kill-criterion's question BY INACTION, and the gate must say so, out loud, in the first line. Two validation-only sprints in a row is a project grooming itself to death (attack #11); V35 is the sprint that makes the kill-criterion answerable — the honest conclusion at V36 is no longer 'validation-only' but 'the Operator has, by inaction, answered'.
haltRePinned.theNumberGoesFirst: the gate's first line is two facts: 'manifests authored (real): <n> · cycles run unprompted on real lineages: <n>' AND 'published: <n> · reachableHumans: <n>' — measured, whatever they are. The number is what it is, and until now exactly one human could have made it otherwise.

adversarialRecord_partA.rule: PART A' — 12 attacks, each with its binding consequence, attacked BEFORE design. The findings_closed_reach wall asserts each consequence holds in the shipped code.

adversarialRecord_partA.A2_mockedCrossCheck: the gravest available failure — a mock converts an honest gap into a lie with a passing test. Consequence: DD-9 forbids vendoring/stubbing/mocking/reimplementing; if it cannot install, S94 stays RED and D33 is pinned UNSIGNABLE anyway.
adversarialRecord_partA.A3_distributionIsCapability: the sharpest attack and it partly LANDS. A binary lets a user run ORGANON without a dev toolchain — that IS reach. Consequence: answered on the Halt's purpose (stop engineering ahead of validation; a binary is the precondition of validation for anyone but the Operator; refusing it makes the Halt self-sealing); the narrowing is taken (binary and nothing else); disclosed D49 unsigned; the Operator may strike it.
adversarialRecord_partA.A4_binaryStillZero: LANDS COMPLETELY — the commit is UNPUSHED and publication is Operator-gated; the binary removes the technical barrier and hits a second unsigned pen. Consequence: the sprint's headline finding — reachableHumans = published ? UNJUDGEABLE : 1; shipping the binary does not create reach, PUBLISHING it does; the gate carries TWO pens (IN2 and PUBLICATION).
adversarialRecord_partA.A5_deferralIsCowardice: fair, answered structurally: D50 is hash-pinned WITH its ending condition (binary AND install AND published AND a stated window) — a pre-registered exit criterion, not a dodge.
adversarialRecord_partA.A6_grepWallForGreen: LANDS, the irony is total (the substring advice guard all over again). Consequence: X-REACH(c) — green is a DERIVED VALUE, never a typed word; the marker's verify slot is {exitCode, subchecks[]}.
adversarialRecord_partA.A7_jitterIsNotDeterminism: LANDS — X-DETERM admits no tolerance. Consequence: DD-11/S99 — exact or excluded with a reason; a band is forbidden; two runs identical expect().
adversarialRecord_partA.A8_binaryShipsTheSinks: a genuine, newly-created security risk — the binary makes V34's seal load-bearing for third parties. Consequence: DD-13's three hardening assertions walled (S96) — no key, no provider on offline first run, console disabled without the flag; if any fails, the binary does not ship and the reason is named.
adversarialRecord_partA.A9_reachIsAMadeUpNumber: valid; every vanity metric starts as an estimate. Consequence: X-REACH(e) — reach is STRUCTURAL, never surveyed; reachableHumans = published ? UNJUDGEABLE : 1; ORGANON says UNJUDGEABLE exactly as it does for a missing peg.
adversarialRecord_partA.A10_censusWhitewash: valid — dropping walls that cannot have a negative is how a census becomes a whitewash. Consequence: the EXEMPT bucket is enumerated, reasoned, and COUNTED in the marker; a rising exempt count is itself a finding.
adversarialRecord_partA.A11_groomingToDeath: true, said out loud — two validation-only sprints is a project grooming itself to death. Consequence: D50's ending condition and the gate's TWO pens; if V36 opens with IN2 unperformed and the tree unpublished, the Operator has answered by inaction, and the gate says so.
adversarialRecord_partA.A12_priorityInversion: valid — fixing verify and the census while the frozen core's math is unverified. Consequence: PHASE 1 IS THE CROSS-CHECK AND IT NEVER SHEDS; shed order pinned (Phase 1 never · Phase 4 first · then 5 · then 3).

postImplementationRePins_partF.rule: PART F — design defects found before code, blocking re-pins for Phase 0 (the RP-1..RP-4 mechanism from V34, two of which were that sprint's most valuable corrections).
postImplementationRePins_partF.RP1_censusOriginUnrecorded: CRITICAL — the census would pass while proving almost nothing because 'the original defect' is undefined for two-thirds of the walls; an agent would invent an origin retroactively (indistinguishable from an arbitrary mutation dressed up). Fix: split the census — WALLS WITH A RECORDED ORIGIN (defect quoted from the build log; the negative reproduces THAT defect) vs WALLS WITHOUT (ORIGIN-UNRECORDED, a fourth counted bucket, expected to be large, shown negatives explicitly NOT-PROVEN-original).
postImplementationRePins_partF.RP2_purgedcvRealBlocker: HIGH — purgedcv may not be the real blocker; the sprint could fix the wrong thing. V34 said BLOCKED (purgedcv absent, Py3.11-only) but V33 claimed a Py3.11.15 rebuild. Determined this sprint: possibility (i)+(iii) — the studio slim venv is built from requirements-studio.txt (numpy+scipy ONLY); purgedcv==0.1.2 lives in the PARKED heavy requirements.txt, so the cross-check was never installable via the standard setup path AND does not persist across a fresh clone. The real fix is NOT a one-off install: commit the cross-check requirement + a bootstrap so the check survives a fresh clone; the marker states which of the three was true.
postImplementationRePins_partF.RP3_egressAssertionStrength: HIGH — 'zero egress on first run' is not testable as an unqualified negative (proving no network activity needs a deny-egress sandbox or platform-specific tracing; a 'no fetch was called' test says nothing about the runtime or a transitive fetch). Fix: state the assertion at the strength it can be PROVEN — the first-run path executes with ORGANON_OFFLINE=1 and NO provider is constructed; a seeded provider construction on the fixture path FAILS; the SBOM shows two leaf components with zero transitive deps, so there is no third-party code that could egress. 'Zero egress' unqualified would be NOT HELD (X-SHOWN(b)).
postImplementationRePins_partF.RP4_publishedDerived: MEDIUM-HIGH — the reach fact hard-codes published:false and will silently lie the day it is published. Fix: published is DERIVED, not declared — from the git remote state (does a remote ref contain this commit?). A declared published flag is the X-RECKON defect reintroduced in a new field (that the blueprint reintroduced it is itself evidence of how easy the mistake is).
postImplementationRePins_partF.RP5_statedWindow: MEDIUM — D50's 'a stated observation window' is unspecified; an unspecified window is an infinitely deferrable deferral. Fix: the window is stated NOW as a number — 90 days from the publication commit, or 30 days from the first external clone, whichever is sooner. The Operator may amend it, but a deferral without a date is an evasion.
postImplementationRePins_partF.RP6_censusRegeneratedByBattery: MEDIUM — the census is a snapshot and will rot as the golden-move discipline rotted. Fix: Falsify.census() is a pure read over the wall catalog; a wall added without a bucket assignment FAILS the battery on the next run. A living wall, not a document.
postImplementationRePins_partF.RP7_lawCountShown: MEDIUM, structural (F-7) — two validation-only sprints have produced no product change and the constitution now has sixteen laws; the project has no instrument to tell deepening from calcifying. Fix (observation): the gate reports laws:16 · minted in last 5 sprints:5 · product capability added in last 2 sprints:0, side by side, before the pen.
